newsitem.title: USA: Tax proposal would aid California counties, cities.
newsitem.headline: Tax proposal would aid California counties, cities.

text.p: Two California state Assembly members introduced legislation that would aid financially troubled local governments by reducing their property tax shifts to the state, aides said Wednesday.
Under the legislation, the shift of local property tax funds to the so-called Educational Revenue Augmentation Fund would be reduced by 10 percent for the upcoming budget year.
The change was proposed by Allies for California's Cities and Counties. Legislation was formally introduced by state Assembly members Michael Sweeney and Fred Aguiar, their aides said.

The state's financial crisis during the 1992-1993 and 1993-1994 fiscal years led to the creation of the Educational Revenue Augmentation Fund, which used local property taxes to bolster school funding.
The tax shift amounts to $3.6 billion a year but increases as assessed valuation grows, the coalition said.

Under the proposal, local governments would retain the growth in property tax revenues, providing localities an estimated $100 million in the 1997-1998 fiscal year, according to Douglas Elmets, the coalition's spokesman.

"We hope the governor and Legislature understand that the fiscal situation for cities and counties had deteriorated even further and that they will act quickly to give local governments the relief they need," Elmets said.
Similar legislation was passed by the state Legislature last year, but was vetoed by Gov. Pete Wilson, a Republican.
